verdict_line: A record 79.9% operating ratio that the CEO attributes to AI, with in-house capability beating its own productivity targets. No problem to solve in North America. The only soft spot is Europe, where restructuring pushed the segment to a loss.

thesis.text: They are winning, and they are winning with AI. North American LTL adjusted operating ratio improved 300 basis points to a record 79.9%, AI workforce-planning technology contributed roughly 2.5 productivity points against a 1.5-point target.

The financials are excellent. Revenue $2.36 billion (+13.2%), adjusted diluted EPS $1.70 (+61.9%), adjusted EBITDA $434 million (+25% excluding real estate), free cash flow $207 million, net leverage 2.1x.

Pricing power is real — XPO reports pricing two to three points above competitors on the strength of service and technology investment, and has raised full-year OR-improvement guidance to at least 200 basis points against a low-70s long-term target.

Europe is the exception. The European Transportation segment posted a $6 million operating loss against $11 million of income a year earlier, driven by restructuring, though adjusted EBITDA still rose to $48 million.

exhibits.title: Performance
exhibits.headline: Record LTL operating ratio and adjusted EPS up 62% — with a European segment in restructuring.
exhibits.body_html: Revenue $2,355 million (+13.2%), GAAP diluted EPS $1.36 (from $0.89), adjusted diluted EPS $1.70 (+61.9%), adjusted EBITDA $434 million. North American LTL revenue $1.43 billion (+15.2%) with adjusted operating ratio at a record 79.9%, improved 300 basis points. European Transportation revenue $927 million (+10%) with a $6 million operating loss. Free cash flow $207 million, cash $298 million, net leverage 2.1x. Q3 LTL operating ratio expected below 81%. CEO: Mario Harik.
exhibits.sowhat: Approaching XPO with an efficiency pitch would be embarrassing — they are the ones setting the benchmark. If an opening exists it is European restructuring and systems rationalisation, not North American operations. Revisit at Q3.
